summary: Round 2 of M4.19, verified by mutation against the staged bytes (Invariants.java restored byte-for-byte afterwards; staged hash re-checked as 80b3346b, all four untracked M4.16/M4.20 files left in place, probe class deleted). Round-1 finding 3 is CLOSED and closed well: M4.21 exists at backlog.md:268 and its description is accurate against the script -- check-reviewed.sh calls `finish` at line 49 inside the `ROUNDS > 2` block (42-50), ahead of the baselines-reading loop at line 52, and that loop keys `<role>:<id>` over blocking/major findings only, so a round-count key could never have been consumed by it. Withdrawing the baselines/review.txt entry was the right call rather than a loss of evidence: the entry was inert against the gate whose message invited it, the file's own header scopes it to 'findings argued as non-defects', and the M4.21 row now carries the whole narrative including the 12-round M4.12 instance and the stated SKIP. Round-1 findings 1 and 2 are fixed in the CODE but the fixes are not pinned by the fixtures that were added for them, and both survive mutation with the entire sequencer suite green -- measured, not inferred. That is R2-1 and R2-2 below. Per review.md rule 12 these do not buy a round 3: the remedy I would prefer is to split the `Report`/`examine` addition and its fixture out of M4.19 into their own row, since that is the surface round 2's fix created and it is separable from the six predicates the row legitimately delivers. Cost lens: the diff touches no production path (both new files are under sequencer/src/test/java) so no billed object-store request rate changes; the harness-side read count is noted as a minor against M4.13's stated 60 s budget. Six of the row's claimed falsifiable predicates I re-verified by hand: the seal-bounded fold IS falsifiable in both directions (`upTo = Long.MAX_VALUE` and the missing `break` each fail offsetsBEYONDThePredecessorsSEALAreNOTInherited).

findings.title: Report's counters are DECLARED, not derived -- both can be hard-coded with the suite green, and boundariesFollowed has no reader anywhere in the tree
findings.failure_scenario: MEASURED. Replacing Invariants.java:101 `return new Report(found, entries.size(), boundaries[0]);` with `return new Report(found, entries.isEmpty() ? 0 : 2, 0);` -- i.e. a two-valued literal for entriesExamined and a bare literal 0 for boundariesFollowed -- leaves `./gradlew :sequencer:test --rerun-tasks` BUILD SUCCESSFUL. Separately, deleting `boundaries[0] += 1;` at Invariants.java:292 outright also leaves the whole sequencer suite green, and `grep -rn boundariesFollowed` over the repository matches only its own declaration: nothing asserts it, nothing reads it, and the untracked CommitProtocolSimulation calls `checkChain` rather than `examine`, so it has no consumer either. The Report javadoc at Invariants.java:87-90 states the opposite in bold -- 'DERIVED, NOT DECLARED ... These counts come from the walk, so gutting the walk drives them to zero' -- and that sentence is false in both halves. entriesExamined comes from `readChain`, not from the walk, so gutting the whole `check` loop leaves it at 2; and I measured a chain at epoch 41 whose examination read 41 chains and reported `entriesExamined=2`, so it does not answer 'how much did you examine' -- it reports the size of the one chain addressed. CONCRETE FAILURE: the counter exists to make round-1's defect visible, and it cannot. If the cross-boundary walk-back is later broken -- the exact mutation round 1 measured, production `open(prevEpoch, 0)` -- `boundariesFollowed` silently becomes 0, `checkChain` returns `[]`, M4.13's sweep is green, and there is now a number present making that look examined. This is the shape of `crossEpochOffsetsChecked()`, deleted three paragraphs above in the same file for being 'a claim that cannot go false', reintroduced one step milder. Minimum: assert `boundariesFollowed` in anABSENTChainIsReportedAsUNEXAMINEDRatherThanClean (the fork and never-opened fixtures already build multi-hop shapes where it is 1 and 2 respectively -- I measured both), and either derive entriesExamined from the walk as the javadoc claims or correct the javadoc to say it is the addressed chain's entry count.

findings.title: The second-seal fixture asserts only isNotEmpty(), so EACH of the two first-seal-wins fixes survives alone -- including the upTo fold, which is the arm that does the masking
findings.failure_scenario: MEASURED, three mutations. (a) Reverting ONLY the `upTo` scan at Invariants.java:281-287 to last-seal-wins (drop the `break`): `./gradlew :sequencer:test --rerun-tasks` BUILD SUCCESSFUL. (b) Reverting ONLY the `checkLink` scan at Invariants.java:350-356 to last-seal-wins: BUILD SUCCESSFUL. (c) Reverting BOTH: aSECONDSealPastAFencedWritersDeltaDoesNOTMoveTheBarrier FAILED. So the fixture round 2 added for this finding constrains the CONJUNCTION of the two changes and neither of them individually. The mechanism is the assertion: `assertThat(found).isNotEmpty()` is satisfied by either arm firing, and with (a) applied checkLink still reports a `link` violation for the `continuedAt`/`prevSeq` mismatch, while with (b) applied the seal-bounded fold still reports a `gap`. CONCRETE FAILURE: the arm that matters is the `upTo` fold, because that is the one that decides whether a fenced writer's five offsets are INHERITED -- the masking the round-1 finding named verbatim ('folding to the LAST one inherits everything a fenced writer appended between the two'). A future edit that folds to the last seal again -- or that reorders the loop so `break` is unreachable -- reintroduces exactly the measured defect (epoch 3 resuming at 8 past the real barrier at slot 2) with the sweep green and with a fixture in the file whose name claims to pin it. Fix: assert the violations by kind, not by emptiness -- the fold arm should be pinned by a shape where checkLink is silent (a CONTINUE naming the FIRST seal's slot, so `continuedAt` and `prevSeq` both agree, with a second seal and a fenced delta between them), so that only the fold can produce the report.

findings.title: The empty-chain early return added for minor 6 does hide a genuinely unsealed predecessor, and no fixture pins it in either direction
findings.failure_scenario: MEASURED with a throwaway probe on the staged bytes. Shape: epoch 1 = Continue(0,0,0) + delta(1, 5 records, first=0) and NO SEAL -- an abandoned leader whose writer met no barrier; epoch 2 = absent entirely (acquired and died before its first PUT, which the early return's own comment cites as routine under M4.12's injector); epoch 3 = Continue(0, 2, 0) + delta resuming correctly at 5. `Invariants.checkChain` returns `[]` and `examine` returns `Report[violations=[], entriesExamined=2, boundariesFollowed=1]`. Before the fix this reported a `link` violation, so the fix converted a report into silence for the M4.16 shape -- the one this class was split out of M4.12 to detect. The reason it goes unreported is structural rather than local: `checkLink` is only ever applied to the epoch the CONTINUE NAMES (Invariants.java:263), never to the epoch the never-opened walk-back at 271-274 actually lands on and inherits from, so an unsealed ancestor is invisible whenever one or more epochs were skipped -- which M4.16's row records as the normal case ('ancestors skipped in RUNS rather than singly'). I confirmed the adjacent pre-existing hole too: with epoch 2 present as a never-opened Seal(0, 3) instead of absent, checkChain is also `[]`. This is a reduction in detection power rather than a wrong answer -- the I2 arm still fires once the zombie actually rewinds, which is how the sweep finds it today -- but M4.16's row records seed 79 as violating with ZERO successful zombie writes, and in that case the unsealed precondition is the only signal there is. Also measured: DELETING the `named.isEmpty()` early return leaves the whole sequencer suite green, so the trade the fix made is unconstrained in both directions and undisclosed in the backlog row.

findings.title: The comment argues against the depth cap sitting two lines beneath it, and the cap silently returns an EMPTY inheritance -- which masks I2 rather than reporting anything
findings.failure_scenario: The comment added for minor 4 says 'The depth cap that used to stand here is worse than useless: ChainReplay's javadoc records it as measured-FALSE at 1,002 legitimate terms', and then `if (depth > 1000) { return inherited; }` stands at lines 222-224. I verified the cited measurement: ChainReplay.java:130-135 records that an earlier draft capped depth at 1000, that this was FALSE and measured so, and that production removed it in favour of the strictly-decreasing-epoch rule. So the checker keeps the exact line its own comment calls worse than useless. The failure mode is worse than production's was: production THREW, this returns an empty map silently, so a chain whose ancestry runs past 1,000 opened terms inherits nothing, its first delta reads as a fresh start, and a genuine rewind below the true high-water mark is reported as CLEAN -- the masking this class exists to prevent, arriving from the backstop. Not reachable in M4.13's sweep at ~85 commits per seed, which is why this is minor rather than major, but 'a healthy long-lived cluster' is precisely the case ChainReplay's javadoc says the cap gets wrong. If the strictly-decreasing rule is the termination argument (it is: `from` strictly decreases and is floored at 1, so the recursion terminates without the cap), delete the cap; if it is kept, it must report rather than return silently.

findings.title: The strictly-decreasing-epoch predicate added for minor 4 has no fixture -- deleting it leaves the suite green
findings.failure_scenario: MEASURED: removing the whole `if (entries.getFirst() instanceof Continue link && link.prevEpoch() >= epoch)` block leaves `./gradlew :sequencer:test --rerun-tasks` BUILD SUCCESSFUL. No fixture in InvariantsTest builds a CONTINUE whose prevEpoch is greater than or equal to its own epoch -- every `new Continue(...)` in the file names a strictly lower epoch -- so the new `chain` violation is an arm nothing can break, in a class whose row's whole remaining deliverable was 'the count is the argument: four predicates ... each survive deletion with the whole suite green'. The fix for a minor therefore added a seventh predicate with the same defect the row was opened to close. This is what review.md rule 11 warns about ('fixing a minor is permitted and usually wrong, because the new round's surface is the prose the fix just added'); the honest options are a two-object-cycle fixture asserting `chain`, or reverting to the depth cap alone and leaving the original minor recorded in the commit body.

findings.title: The M4.19 row's DELIVERED paragraph describes round 1's fixes only, and retains the pre-fix open-findings sentence as though still open
findings.failure_scenario: The row now reads '... the I2 rewind boundary is unpinned by one record, crossEpochOffsetsChecked() is a hard-coded true with an assertion around it, and two fixtures build a LeaseManager on Clock.systemUTC() ... ⚠️ DELIVERED' -- the stale open-findings clause is left standing and the resolution appended after it, so a reader meets three open defects and then a paragraph that answers only some of them. More substantively, nothing round 2 added is in the row: not `Invariants.Report` or `examine` (a new public API), not the first-seal-vs-last-seal correction (which the row would need in order for a later reader to know why two loops break), not the strictly-decreasing-epoch check, and not the `checkLink` empty-chain early return that changed what the checker reports for an absent predecessor. This is the defect the row itself names twice -- 'an earlier draft of this row described a commit other than itself' and 'a round's fix adds a file and the list is not extended' -- recurring by the same mechanism. The consequence is concrete for M4.13: its author will read this row to learn what the checker does and does not check, and the row does not say that the `upTo` fold and `checkLink` now agree on the FIRST seal, nor that an absent named predecessor is deliberately not reported.

findings.title: Harness-side read count grows with the square of epochs burned, and ancestor violations are re-reported once per descendant
findings.failure_scenario: No production path is touched, so no billed request rate changes -- both new files are under sequencer/src/test/java and the diff adds no get/put/list to the ingester or plugin. Inside the harness, though: `readChain` issues one LIST per 1000 objects plus one GET per entry, `firstAncestorWithDeltas` reads the FULL chain of every epoch from `epoch - 1` down to 1, and the untracked CommitProtocolSimulation calls `checkChain` once per epoch -- so a sweep over E epochs performs O(E^2) reads. MEASURED: a single `examine` of an epoch-5000 chain whose CONTINUE claims no predecessor issues ~4,999 LISTs (17 ms against MemoryBinStore). M4.16 records 73 epochs burned per 3 takeovers and M4.13 states a budget of under 60 s for 1,000 seeds, so this is the term that will decide whether that budget holds; it belongs in M4.13's row rather than being discovered when the sweep is slow. Second, smaller point: `inheritedOffsets` appends to the caller's `found` list, so one broken link at epoch k is reported once for every descendant epoch subsequently examined, inflating the counts M4.13 is meant to pin as 'exactly the known-failing seeds and no others'.
